checklist.detail: The exact retained binary reported grok 1.0.40 (eb1a2256660d) [stable] before the run. The host default had advanced to 1.0.41 (4220f3b224a6), so this receipt names the exact 1.0.40 executable validated.
The production launch emitted --permission-mode bypassPermissions and the transcript recorded yolo_mode=true.
PtyConfig emitted a fresh bare UUID through both --session-id and CAS_SESSION_ID; the same ID named the live transcript.
The production launch emitted grok-4.5 with medium reasoning effort and the assistant transcript recorded both.
Both the process cwd and --cwd targeted the disposable repository; prompt_context.json recorded the same working directory.
The production --rules payload contained the Cassy Factory Worker role and cas__ namespace, and the exact text appeared in system_prompt.txt.
Persistent config discovered cas serve, connected 15 tools, and the worker invoked cas__coordination and cas__task rather than Claude/Codex aliases.
Inherited CAS agent, role, factory, session, root, worker CLI, model, and effort environment bound cas serve to the disposable store and registered the expected Grok worker.
The session was written under ~/.grok/sessions/*/<session-id>; its post-submit turn_ended event cleared Pane in-flight state through the production liveness resolver.
The worker called whoami, mine, show, start, and notes; wrote the exact probe marker; committed it with the versioned lifecycle subject; and left the disposable repository clean.
Grok inspect reported every discovered Claude/Cursor-compatible hook disabled, and the SessionStart hook canary did not execute.
The worker wrote and committed only the named probe in the disposable repository; git status was clean afterward and the production --cwd/prompt context remained inside that repository.

A mid-turn sleep probe was interrupted through Mux::interrupt_and_inject; Cassy's Grok turn-break path sent Ctrl+C and the redirected turn completed with CAS-GROK-1.0.40-INTERRUPTED-OK. This confirms the 1.0.24 Esc decision note without treating Esc itself as the turn-break byte.

Not covered: this bounded non-interactive matrix used the persistent stdio Cassy server, which did not request additional input; it did not provision a synthetic MCP tool that pauses for a form answer and resumes.
Not covered: no MCP server in the isolated configuration requested URL consent or question-form input, so the interactive consent popup path was not exercised.
Not covered: the run did not enable or configure Grok model-context memory; it validated the standard --rules and cas__ discovery path only.
Not covered: the bounded worker lifecycle and urgent-interrupt turns completed below compaction pressure; no forced long-session compaction was attempted.

evidence.summary: Fresh real Grok Build 1.0.40 PtyConfig::grok run with target/debug/cas first on PATH, a disposable repository/CAS_ROOT, compatible hooks disabled, persistent cas__ MCP discovery, worker lifecycle, and urgent interrupt redirect; all required assertions passed.
